e: A member of the US Marine Corps is arrested on suspicion of murdering a woman in Naha, Okinawa Prefecture.
The government raises the permanent foreign residency fee to 200,000 yen ($1,270) and introduces new requirements for the status.
Four people are killed while six others are reported missing in Chiba and Kanagawa Prefectures following incidents caused by Typhoon Dujuan.
Prime Minister Takaichi conducts a cabinet reshuffle.
Twenty-four students are injured following a tear gas spraying incident at Osaka University of Commerce - Sakai High School in Naka-ku, Sakai, Osaka Prefecture.
A bus and truck collide in Nada-ku, Kobe, Hyogo Prefecture, injuring at least 10 people.
A Northrop Grumman RQ-4 Global Hawk of the Japan Air Self-Defense Force crashes into the Sea of Japan off Tottori Prefecture.
Flooding and landslides caused by heavy rains leave one person dead in Kawanehon, Shizuoka prefecture, and 41 others injured in Nagoya.
A suspected arson of a cake shop in Motosu, Gifu Prefecture kills three people and injures two.
A fishing boat sinks in Nichinan, Miyazaki Prefecture, killing three people.
Japanese researcher Tokuji Unno wins the Ig Nobel Prize for his 1977 paper “How to Blow the Nose — An Aerodynamic Study of the Nose Blowing.”
A fire breaks out in a shopping arcade in Ise, Mie Prefecture.
Takeharu Yamanaka resigns as mayor of Yokohama after he admits to subjecting city employees to bullying and verbal abuse.
Three middle schoolers are washed away offshore and are missing in Ichikikushikino, Kagoshima Prefecture.
Typhoon Saudel (Typhoon No. 18) hits Okinawa Prefecture, injuring three people.
Four luxury watches valued at 200 million yen ($1.2 million) are stolen from a watch store in Nakano, Tokyo.
A leisure boat collides with a seawall near Haneda Airport, injuring nine people.
A magnitude 5.9 earthquake strikes southern Ibaraki Prefecture injuring 45 people.
Sunao Takami, who killed five people in a 2009 arson attack at a pachinko shop in Konohana-ku, Osaka, becomes the first person to be executed under the Takaichi administration.
Four railway workers at the Tōbu Nikkō Line die after being struck by a limited express train in Shin-Kanuma Station in Kanuma, Tochigi.
The United States imposes sanctions on Japanese jurist Tomoko Akane, citing her position as president of the International Criminal Court.
Thirteen people are killed following record-breaking heavy rainfall and flooding in Chiba Prefecture.
A law penalizing the desecration of the Japanese flag comes into effect.
Severe Tropical Storm Chan-hom (Typhoon No. 15) makes landfall on Ibaraki Prefecture, the first time since records began in 1951. Two people are injured.
A knife-wielding man is shot dead by police in Kawachinagano, Osaka Prefecture.
Twelve people are injured in an apartment fire in Koganei, Tokyo.
A magnitude 7.1 earthquake hits Kumamoto Prefecture, killing 39 people.
The ancient capital of Asuka-Fujiwara is designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The United States imposes a 12.5% tariff on Japan, citing the presence of alleged forced labour in the supply chain.
A fire breaks out in Camp Asaka.
Twenty-three people, including 18 students, are hospitalized following a spraying incident in Municipal Third Middle High School in Kaizuka, Osaka Prefecture.
Japanese imperial succession debate: The House of Councillors passes the "Imperial Family Code" bill.
The government approves the establishment of a new intelligence agency, the National Intelligence Bureau, for the first time since World War II.

Japanese imperial succession debate: The House of Representatives passes the "Imperial Family Code" bill seeking to amend the rights of succession of the Japanese imperial family. Following the passing of the bill, various protests are held by 27,000 people across 136 places in Japan including in front of the National Diet.
Tarō Yamamoto resigned as the leader of Reiwa Shinsengumi.
A house and a road is destroyed following a landslide in Koka, Shiga.
The 2026 Shiga gubernatorial election is held.
A magnitude 5.6 earthquake strikes Yamanashi Prefecture, injuring 10 people.
A magnitude 6.9 earthquake hits off Iwate Prefecture, injuring five people.
At least 15 buildings are burned after a fire breaks out in a shopping arcade in Izumo, Shimane.
